## Restaurant Website Launch Checklist for Pune: Menu, Mobile Speed, Google Listing, Ordering and Food-Licence Details Before You Go Live

Before a Pune restaurant or café launches its website, check six things: the menu is real text that loads fast on a phone; the address, hours and phone number are correct and match your Google Business Profile; the main action (call, reserve, order or WhatsApp) works with one tap; your food-licence details and legal pages are in place; analytics and the search-engine basics are set up; and the site has been tested on real phones, with real orders, before the public sees it. That is the short answer. The rest of this guide turns it into a checklist your developer can follow and you can verify yourself, in the order work is normally done. It is written for owners and managers of restaurants, cafés, bakeries and cloud kitchens who are about to launch a new site or relaunch an old one.

### Who this guide is for

You have a restaurant or café in Pune, or a small group of outlets, and a website is being built, either by a developer, an agency or a site-builder tool. You are not a technical person, and you want to know what to check before saying "go live". If you also want a plan for what to do after launch, our companion guide on [digital marketing for restaurants and cafés](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-restaurant-cafe-marketing-own-channels-2026) covers the next steps.

## Step 1: Decide What the Website Is For

A restaurant website has one or two main jobs, and the design follows from them.

- **Show the place and the food** so a person decides to visit.
- **Take direct action:** call, reserve a table, order for pickup or delivery, or start a WhatsApp chat.
- **Prove you are real:** address, photos, hours and licence details.

Write down the one action you most want a visitor to take and make sure it is possible within two taps on a phone. Everything else supports that. If you are unsure whether you need a full custom site or something simpler, see the comparison in our guide to [WordPress themes versus page builders](/blog/wordpress-theme-vs-page-builder) and the overview of [web development companies in Pune](/blog/web-development-company-pune-guide-2026).

## Step 2: Domain, Hosting and Security

These are the foundations. Get them right once and keep records.

**Domain.**
- Choose a name that is easy to say and type, ideally your restaurant's name with a .in or .com ending. Avoid hyphens and number tricks that are easy to mistype.
- Register the domain in your own (or your company's) name, with your own email as the contact. If the developer registers it in their name, you do not own your address. Our guide to [website handover and ownership](/blog/web-development-company-pune-website-handover-ownership-checklist-2026) explains what you should receive.
- Turn on auto-renewal and record the renewal date. An expired domain takes the site and email down; see our note on [domain, DNS and SSL renewals](/blog/web-development-company-pune-domain-dns-ssl-renewal-website-downtime-2026).

**Hosting.**
- Pick hosting that suits the site's size. A simple menu and booking site does not need an expensive plan, but it should have backups, security updates and support. See our overview of [WordPress hosting options in India](/blog/choose-wordpress-hosting-india).
- Ask where the server is located and whether there is a content delivery network. For a Pune audience, a nearby region helps speed, but a good CDN matters more than the exact city.

**HTTPS.**
- The site must load on https with a valid certificate and redirect plain http to https. Most hosts provide this at no extra cost.
- Check that the www and non-www versions go to one address; see our guide to [canonical URLs and duplicate content](/blog/web-development-company-pune-canonical-urls-duplicate-content-www-https-2026).

**Backups and updates.**
- Confirm automatic daily or weekly backups and that you can restore one; see [website backups and disaster recovery](/blog/web-development-company-pune-website-backups-disaster-recovery-2026).
- If the site uses WordPress, make sure the core software, theme and plugins are current, with two-factor authentication on admin accounts. Our [WordPress security checklist](/blog/wordpress-security-checklist-business) lists the basics.

## Step 3: The Menu — The Page Most Visitors Want

The menu is why most people visit a restaurant website. Treat it as the main product page.

- **Use real text, not a photographed menu or a single PDF.** Text loads fast, resizes on small screens, can be read by screen readers and can be found by search engines. A PDF can be offered as a download in addition.
- **Show prices in rupees,** matching what you charge in the outlet and on any delivery app. A mismatch between website and app prices causes arguments at the counter.
- **Mark dietary information clearly:** vegetarian or non-vegetarian symbols as Indian practice expects, and any major allergens you can state reliably. If you cannot guarantee something, say "ask us" rather than guess.
- **Describe signature dishes briefly** and add a photograph of your own food. Avoid stock photos that do not match what arrives on the plate.
- **Make it easy to update.** Prices and availability change, so a content-management system the staff can edit is better than a developer-only change. Set up an owner and a routine for updates.
- **Mention what is seasonal or limited** so that visitors are not disappointed.

### Optional: menu structured data

Search engines can understand a menu better if the page includes structured data, which is code that describes the content. For restaurants, Google documents markup for the business itself (name, address, hours, cuisine, price range, menu link). Only mark up information that is visible on the page and accurate. Our guides to [structured data for business sites](/blog/web-development-company-pune-structured-data-schema-markup-2026) and [LocalBusiness markup](/blog/web-development-company-pune-localbusiness-schema-nap-opening-hours-2026) explain the legitimate use. Do not add review stars to your own site's pages; Google's guidance on review snippets says that self-controlled reviews for local business markup are not eligible.

## Step 4: Mobile Speed and Design

Most diners will look you up on a phone, often on mobile data, so the site must be fast and easy to use one-handed.

- **Test on real phones,** at least one budget Android handset and one iPhone, on mobile data as well as Wi-Fi.
- **Keep images light.** Use modern formats where supported and compress photographs; our guide to [image optimisation](/blog/website-designer-pune-image-optimization-avif-webp-lcp-2026) explains the options.
- **Use readable text sizes and tappable buttons,** with enough space between them to avoid mistaken taps.
- **Put the key information near the top:** the call button, address, opening hours today, and the primary action.
- **Check Google's Core Web Vitals,** which measure loading, responsiveness and visual stability. You can run PageSpeed Insights on the live page and look at the real-user data where available; see our notes on [Core Web Vitals for WordPress](/blog/wordpress-core-web-vitals-optimization).
- **Avoid autoplay video backgrounds and heavy sliders.** They slow the page and drain data.
- **Check accessibility basics:** text contrast, image descriptions, keyboard use. See [accessibility and Core Web Vitals](/blog/website-accessibility-core-web-vitals-designer-pune-2026).

Embedded maps and videos can be heavy; load them on demand where you can. See [YouTube and Google Maps embeds](/blog/web-development-company-pune-youtube-google-maps-embeds-iframe-performance-2026) for how.

## Step 5: The Main Action — Call, Reserve, Order or WhatsApp

Decide which actions you offer, and make each of them work perfectly.

- **Tap-to-call:** the phone number should be a link that starts a call on mobile. Test it.
- **WhatsApp:** a button that opens a chat with a short pre-filled message, such as "Hi, I would like to book a table for 4 on Saturday". Our guide on [call and WhatsApp buttons](/blog/website-designer-pune-click-to-call-whatsapp-buttons-mobile-service-website-2026) covers the link format and placement. See also our page on [WhatsApp for restaurants](/whatsapp/industries/restaurants-food).
- **Reservations:** if you use a form or a booking tool, make sure confirmations arrive and that your staff see them in one place; see [online appointment booking](/blog/website-designer-pune-online-appointment-booking-service-business-2026) for how the options compare.
- **Online ordering:** if you take direct orders, test the full path, from choosing items to receiving the order in your kitchen. Complete real test orders at different times, with a payment provider you have chosen and configured according to its own documentation, and confirm that the order reaches the right person with the right details. Decide who handles delivery and what area you serve.
- **Forms:** every form should send a clear confirmation to the visitor and a notification to your team, and should be protected from spam. See [contact-form spam protection](/blog/website-designer-pune-contact-form-spam-bot-protection-2026) and, if you use a CRM, [connecting forms to a CRM](/blog/web-development-company-pune-website-form-to-crm-integration-lead-capture-2026).

## Step 6: Legal and Trust Information

Restaurants are regulated businesses, and a website is a public statement. Check each of these with your accountant or adviser for your own situation; rules change, and this guide is not legal advice.

- **Food-licence details.** FSSAI regulates food businesses in India, including how a licence or registration number is shown. Check the current FSSAI requirements for displaying your number, and show it where required, for example on the website's footer or about page, as your adviser recommends.
- **Business identity:** the legal name of the business, address and contact details.
- **Tax details.** If your business is registered for GST, your tax invoices must follow the rules applying to you; confirm with your accountant what your website and ordering system should display. We do not give tax advice here.
- **Privacy notice.** If you collect names, phone numbers or order details, explain what you collect, why, and how people can ask for correction or deletion. India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 applies to personal data processed in digital form. See our guide to [DPDP compliance for business websites](/blog/dpdp-act-website-compliance-pune-2026).
- **Terms for orders and bookings:** cancellation rules, refunds for direct orders and what happens when an item is unavailable. Keep it plain and fair; Indian consumer-protection rules on misleading practices apply, as outlined in our guide on [consumer-protection obligations for online sellers](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-consumer-protection-rules-2026).
- **Cookie notice,** if you use analytics or advertising tools that set cookies; see our guide to [cookie banners and popups](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-popups-exit-offers-cookie-banners-mobile-seo-2026).
- **Offers:** state conditions clearly and avoid pressure tactics that mislead.

## Step 7: Local Search and Google Basics

A new site should be found when someone nearby searches for a place to eat.

- **Google Business Profile.** Claim and verify it, check that the name, address, phone number and hours exactly match the website, and link to the new site. See [local SEO and the map pack in Pune](/blog/local-seo-google-map-pack-pune-2026).
- **Page titles and descriptions.** Give each page a distinct title and a short description that reads naturally, for example "Café in Koregaon Park, Pune: Menu, Hours and Reservations". Do not stuff keywords.
- **One page per outlet,** with its own address, hours, photographs and map. Do not create near-identical pages for every neighbourhood; Google's spam policies treat that as doorway abuse. See [service-area pages and doorway problems](/blog/website-designer-pune-service-area-location-pages-doorway-2026).
- **Sitemap and robots.** Check that a sitemap exists and that the site is not accidentally blocking search engines with a "noindex" setting left from the staging stage. This is a common launch error; our guide on [new sites not appearing on Google](/blog/web-development-company-pune-new-website-not-on-google-crawled-not-indexed-2026) explains how to check.
- **Search Console.** Verify the site in Google Search Console and submit the sitemap.
- **Old addresses.** If this is a relaunch, set up redirects from every old page to its new equivalent, and fix broken links; see [404 errors and redirects](/blog/web-development-company-pune-404-errors-redirects-broken-links-2026) and [site-move redirect maps](/blog/web-development-company-pune-domain-change-site-move-redirect-map-2026).

## Step 8: Analytics and Tracking

Before launch, set up measurement, so that you can learn which channels bring customers.

- Install Google Analytics 4 and set key events for calls, WhatsApp clicks, reservation requests and orders. Our guides on [GA4 conversion tracking](/blog/ga4-conversion-tracking-setup-india) and [campaign tagging](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-utm-tracking-campaign-naming-2026) show how.
- Use a tag manager sparingly and audit what it loads; see [third-party scripts and tag managers](/blog/web-development-company-pune-third-party-scripts-tag-manager-audit-2026).
- Check that the tracking respects your cookie notice.
- Note the date of launch so that you can compare before and after.

## Step 9: Test Before You Launch

Test on a staging copy first (see [staging before launch](/blog/website-staging-before-launch)) and then once on the live site. Use this list.

1. Open every page on two phones and one laptop, in two browsers.
2. Tap every button and link; fix any that fail.
3. Place a test reservation and a test order; confirm that your team receives it and that the customer gets a confirmation.
4. Check opening hours, phone number, address and map link.
5. Read the menu for typos and price errors.
6. Run PageSpeed Insights on the home page and menu page.
7. Check that the site works with images off and on a slow connection.
8. Confirm HTTPS, redirects and that the favicon and social-share preview look right.
9. Confirm the "noindex" setting is off in the live site.
10. Check the legal pages, licence details and privacy notice are present.
11. Have someone who did not build it try to complete the main action without help.

## Step 10: Launch Day and the First 30 Days

- Launch at a quiet time, not on a festival weekend.
- Keep a copy of the old site and a rollback plan.
- Update the website link on Google, Instagram, WhatsApp and delivery-app profiles.
- Announce the site to regulars through channels they have agreed to receive.
- In the first week, check Search Console for errors, review analytics, answer messages quickly and fix issues you find.
- At 30 days, review calls, bookings and orders against what you expected, and plan the next improvements. For the longer-term plan, see our guide to [a 90-day digital marketing plan for a local business](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-first-90-days-local-business-plan-2026).

## Common Launch Mistakes

- A menu that exists only as a photograph or PDF.
- Opening hours that differ between website, Google and apps.
- A booking form that sends emails to a mailbox nobody reads.
- A staging "noindex" setting left on, so Google never lists the site.
- A domain registered in the developer's name.
- No backups, no renewal reminders.
- Heavy images and videos that make the site crawl on mobile data.
- Copying another restaurant's text or photographs.
- Claiming something on the site (an award, a rating, a certification) that you cannot prove.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What should a restaurant website include before it launches?

A fast, text-based menu, accurate address, hours and phone, a clear main action such as call, reserve or order, photographs of your own food, legal and licence details, a privacy notice, analytics, and a verified Google listing. Test it on real phones before launch.

### Do I need to show my FSSAI licence number on my restaurant website?

Food businesses are regulated by FSSAI, and the rules include requirements for displaying licence or registration details. Check the current requirements with FSSAI or your adviser, and place the number where those rules say, such as the footer or about page.

### How long does it take to build a restaurant website?

It depends on the scope. A simple menu-and-contact site is much quicker than a site with online ordering, and delays are most often caused by waiting for content, photographs and approvals. Agree a schedule that includes testing time.

### Should I take online orders on my own website or use delivery apps?

Many restaurants do both: apps for discovery and a direct option for repeat customers. The right mix depends on your margins, which you can calculate from your own statements. Direct ordering needs reliable systems and a plan for delivery.

### Will my website show up on Google straight away?

Not always. After launch, verify the site in Google Search Console, submit a sitemap, keep your Google Business Profile accurate and make sure no "noindex" block remains from testing. Appearing and ranking are different things and both take time.

## Where to Start

Write down your single main action, collect an accurate menu with prices, photographs of your own food and your licence and business details, and agree who will own the domain and hosting. Then work through the steps above in order, test on real phones and launch.
